title: When the mouse enters the overlapping area between area2d and UI, area2d's mouse_enter signal will be triggered an extra time.
body: ### Tested versions v4.5.1-stable v4.5-stable v4.4-stable v4.3-stable v4.2.2-stable ### System information Windows 11 ### Issue description I've encountered a bug where when an Area2D overlaps with a UI element, if my mouse enters the overlapping area from the Area2D, the signals sometimes trigger in the following sequence: area_enter -> area_exit -> UI_enter. However, when the bug occurs, the area_enter signal triggers an extra time: area_enter -> area_exit -> area_enter -> UI_enter. I have a demo project here, where the Sprite2D’s range matches the Area2D’s range. When the mouse enters the Area2D (which also means entering the Sprite2D’s area), the Sprite2D turns red. When the mouse exits the Area2D, the Sprite2D turns white, making it easy to visually observe the bug. Additionally: when a bug occurs, if the mouse exits the UI area, the area2d will trigger an extra mouse_exit, paired with the previously extra triggered mouse_enter. This is clearly incorrect because it results in two pairs of mouse_enter and mouse_exit events. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c41dbe3-7f43-47ee-91e6-f1fd81607d3a ### Steps to reproduce 1. Create an Area2D node.Create a UI node In another CanvasLayer.(recommend using a Button, but other UI nodes like ColorRect will have the same bug). 2. Ensure that the area of the Area2D partially overlaps with the area of the UI. 3. Move the mouse from the Area2D into the overlapping area, and use print statements to check the signal output. Expected: The mouse_enter signal of the Area2D should **not** be triggered additionally when the mouse moves into the overlapping area. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [area-2d&ui-conflict.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23855758/area-2d.ui-conflict.zip)
